mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 6% signals a deepening recession, causing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to be negative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by > 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which negatively impacts earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases risk premiums and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which correlates with improved consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST rises by more than 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating data inconsistency or measurement error; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days are expected to be directionless (no significant directional bias).
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns show a statistically significant directional bias during months when both PAYEMS and UNRATE rise simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% annualized for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 remains below 1% annualized for three consecutive quarters.
